purpose: The snags grouped for the design review session: discuss (a decision is needed) or build (we build it as the prototype shows). none = no change needed. The snags page is generated from this file. Replaces the earlier build-oriented categories (done on a branch, exactly as prototype, like prototype with small differences).

blockers.EUDPA-617: Integrate early-access MDM commodity API into live animals frontend
blockers.EUDPA-616: Add a search type-ahead for choosing commodities, reusable across the journey
blockers.EUDPA-719: Spike: a GOV.UK-compliant way to add transit countries as soon as they are picked

rule.blocked: waits for work outside this release (blockedBy names the Jira tickets)
rule.moved: taken out of design snagging into another theme (movedTo names it)
rule.discuss: main would use a different component from the prototype; the prototype relies on JavaScript or non-standard behaviour with no GOV.UK equivalent or no-JS fallback; it contradicts a ruling, the spec or accessibility; the behaviour (not the styling) differs; or it is an open question only the designers can answer
rule.build: everything else, including differences that are only implementation detail (spacing classes, markup, class names), which are left off the cards

items.said: Cursor should move to the next box when full
items.ruling: Settled 20 Oct: three labelled boxes as drawn, no cursor jump, the whole number kept when typed or pasted in one go
items.todo: Three boxes, each with a visible label, styled as drawn. The cursor never moves on its own: moving focus while someone types fails WCAG 3.2.2 unless users are told first, and GOV.UK forms don't do it. Today typing all 9 digits straight through keeps only '12'. The boxes will stop cutting typing short, and the server splits a whole number typed or pasted into the first box. That works without JavaScript.
items.note: The designers' prototype still moves the cursor to the next box. It should drop the jump so it matches.
